gap: No result ChatGPT got states what each kit's panels cost on the maker's own store, worked out as kit price minus the bare station's price, per panel watt. Anker's C2000 Gen 2 + 400 W costs $2.00 per panel watt ($800 more than the station), BLUETTI's Elite 200 V2 kits cost $1.50, EcoFlow's DELTA 2 Max + 2 × 220 W costs $1.25 and Jackery's $1,239 Solar Generator 2000 v2 costs $1.20.
standout_why: PowerSized's kit guide (cited in all three chats) already works out refill hours from each kit's own panels, using 75% of panel watts capped at the station's input (Explorer 2000 v2 + 2 × 200 W comes out at about 7 h). Our refill column is not new. PowerSized gives kit prices but never takes the bare-station price away from them, and it gives no $/Wh for any 2 kWh kit (its only one is $0.59/Wh for an AC180 kit). The Outage Brief gives $/Wh for bare stations only and says it has no information on kits. Unplugged Watts would not load (certificate error), so I could not check it. None of the pages I read prices the panels inside a kit or prices the Anker C2000 Gen 2 + 400 W kit at Anker's own store ($1,999.99). ChatGPT quoted that kit at $1,499.99 from Mighty Generators.
decides: The panel cost per watt backs the BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 + 2 × 200 W ($1,499) and the EcoFlow DELTA 2 Max + 2 × 220 W ($1,579) as the value kits with 400 W or more of panels. It also shows that Anker's own C2000 Gen 2 + 400 W kit is the worst deal in the group: $800 for a 400 W panel, and $600 for a 200 W panel in the bifacial kit. A shopper who wants the Anker should buy it from a reseller, as ChatGPT did, not from Anker's kit page. Jackery's $1,239 kit has the cheapest panels per watt ($1.20/W), but they are only 200 W and the kit is pre-order only (ships Nov 16).
